parsed.explanation: No law criminalises same-sex conduct or gender expression, no prosecutions under the ambiguous age-of-consent article are documented, and reported violence is punished — all positives. But there is no anti-discrimination or hate-crime route, no data protection for gender identity, and police are documented using morality law as a bribery pretext against gender-nonconforming people; 73% of capital residents would dislike a homosexual neighbour. Nothing trans-specific is documented: no border practice, no facility or custody rule, no trans visitor incident. This is thin data on a state that does not criminalise but offers no recourse and shows documented police predation and hostile society. Rated as documented societal hostility with thin recourse plus a corruption lever, mitigated by absence of criminalisation and functioning response to reported violence.

entry_documents.exposure: No documented trans-specific border practice; a marker/presentation mismatch has no local correction route, and no reported refusal-of-entry or secondary-screening pattern.
entry_documents.protection: Entry is not conditioned on gender-marker congruence in any documented rule; data-protection decree covers air-passenger data for sexual orientation.
entry_documents.interaction: Mismatch at a checkpoint could hand an officer the same discretionary lever documented in street bribery; unproven at the border.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: No documented detention or custody-placement practice for trans visitors. Article 331 (same-sex acts under 21) is unprosecuted but invoked as a bribery pretext.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: No known arrests or prosecutions under the provision in 2023; abuses are investigated when reported.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Corrupt officers may escalate a document or presentation query into extortion rather than charge.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: No documented facility-access, bathroom, ward or prison-placement rule applied to trans visitors.

care_services.exposure: No gender-identity anti-discrimination coverage in health, education, housing or employment; no documented refusal aimed at trans visitors.
care_services.interaction: Absence of statutory recourse means a service refusal has no complaint route.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Morality/‘acts against nature’ framing persists; police falsely claim same-sex activity is illegal to extract money; legal protections exclude gender identity.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: No criminalisation of consensual conduct or expression; no arrests recorded.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: State framing is discriminatory rather than threatening: no universal-exposure measure documented.

minors_guardians.exposure: Documented LGBTQ violence is mostly family-perpetrated, which reaches a minor travelling with relatives; no minor-specific rule documented.
minors_guardians.protection: Reported violence is punished; no trans-specific child protective provision documented.
minors_guardians.interaction: Risk concentrates in family/diaspora settings rather than public institutions.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Harassment, physical violence and extortion by state and non-state actors documented; 73% of capital respondents would dislike a homosexual neighbour; trend worsening in 2022.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Where violence is reported, law enforcement punishes it; no hate-crime statute.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Hostility is societal (tier 3) with thin recourse, not state-directed targeting.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No anti-discrimination law, no hate-crime route, no gender-identity data protection; complaints rare for fear of police.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Police act on reported violence; data-protection law covers sexual orientation.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Recourse exists for violence but not for discrimination or extortion; oversight is not documented as operating for trans people.

anchor_checks.comparison: Higher: Vellandra runs a state register barring trans visitors, an enforced universal exclusion. Here no criminalisation, no entry bar, no agency targeting trans travellers is documented; exposure is discretionary corruption and societal hostility instead.

Slightly lower or similar: Kestrel Isles documents actual border secondary screening and refused admission for document mismatch. This dossier documents no border practice at all, so the known exposure is weaker but the surrounding hostility and lack of recourse are comparable; the unknowns cut against the visitor.

Much lower: Meridia documents trained border officers, tribunal appeals, and compensation for unlawful holding. Here there is no anti-discrimination law, no hate-crime route and no gender-identity data protection, so no operative remedy for a trans visitor exists.

Higher: Meridia documents police extortion of trans travellers with overnight cells and document confiscation. Here extortion is documented against men perceived as gay generally, with no trans traveller detention documented, so severity of the operative practice is lower.

parsed.synthesis: The combined regime is one of decriminalisation without protection: no statute targets gender expression, no prosecutions are recorded, and reported violence is punished, but there is no anti-discrimination, hate-crime or gender-identity data protection, police use morality law as a bribery lever against gender-nonconforming people, and capital-area attitudes are strongly hostile. Trans-specific evidence (border, facilities, custody, care) is absent, so the rating extrapolates from the wider legal and social regime: hostile society with thin recourse, a police corruption exposure, and no documented state-imposed universal measure. Rule of law working for victims of violence offsets somewhat; it does not offset the missing recourse for discrimination or extortion.
